questions.text: Prevention of Bribery in Service Delivery: Stopping 'Kitua Kidogo': (1) Cashless payment mandate; (2) CCTV monitoring of centers; (3) Whistleblower channels for citizens; (4) Rotation of staff (to break cartels); (5) Automated queue management; (6) Prosecution of corrupt officials; (7) Public awareness campaigns.
questions.evidence_required: Corruption perception surveys, Prosecution stats, Cashless transaction logs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Petty corruption (bribes for ID) is endemic. Digitization helps, but human 'brokers' often adapt.

questions.text: Procurement Integrity: Clean tenders: (1) Open contracting standards; (2) Beneficial ownership disclosure of vendors; (3) Conflict of interest declarations; (4) Independent audit of tenders; (5) Debarment of corrupt firms; (6) Value for money analysis; (7) Prevention of 'Emergency Procurement' abuse.
questions.evidence_required: Tender audit reports, Conflict of interest forms, Debarment list
questions.africa_specific_notes: ID projects are multi-million dollar honeypots. 'Emergency' procurement often used to bypass rules.

questions.text: Voter Register Integrity: Fair elections: (1) Independence of ID authority from Electoral Commission; (2) Prevention of gerrymandering using ID data; (3) Audit of voter register against civil registry; (4) Transparency of de-duplication; (5) Equal access to ID in opposition strongholds; (6) Observer access to data; (7) Dispute resolution.
questions.evidence_required: Voter register audit, Registration stats by region, Observer reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: In many countries, 'no ID = no vote'. Suppressing ID issuance in opposition areas is a rigging tactic.

questions.text: Surveillance & Political Targeting: Human rights: (1) Legal safeguards against surveillance; (2) Judicial warrant requirement for interception; (3) Protection of journalists/activists; (4) Transparency reports on state requests; (5) Ban on facial recognition in protests; (6) Oversight of intelligence agencies; (7) Redress for illegal surveillance.
questions.evidence_required: Surveillance laws, Court warrants, Transparency reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digital ID + CCTV + AI = Total Surveillance state risk. Activists often targeted.

questions.text: Project Financing & Debt Transparency: Cost of the system: (1) Disclosure of loan terms (interest/conditions); (2) Cost-benefit analysis; (3) Sustainability of debt; (4) Hidden costs (maintenance/licenses); (5) Parliamentary approval of loans; (6) Sovereign guarantee transparency; (7) Impact on national debt.
questions.evidence_required: Loan agreements, Parliamentary hansard, Debt sustainability analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: ID projects often funded by opaque loans. Citizens pay the debt for decades.

questions.text: Revenue Management (e-Services): Where do the fees go?: (1) Treasury Single Account (TSA) usage; (2) Prevention of revenue leakage at source; (3) Audit of e-service revenues; (4) Reconciliation with bank statements; (5) Utilization of funds (re-invested?); (6) Transparency of convenience fees; (7) Agent commission structure.
questions.evidence_required: TSA reports, Revenue audits, Bank reconciliation
questions.africa_specific_notes: e-Government increases revenue collection, but funds must reach the Treasury, not diverted.

questions.text: Ethical Use of Data: Do no harm: (1) Prohibition of data sale to private sector (without consent); (2) Protection of vulnerable groups (refugees/HIV status); (3) Ethical AI guidelines; (4) Benefit sharing (if data monetized); (5) Right to opt-out of secondary uses; (6) Data minimization principle; (7) Impact assessment on marginalized.
questions.evidence_required: Data ethics policy, Impact assessments, Data sale contracts (if any)
questions.africa_specific_notes: Refugee data is highly sensitive. Selling citizen data to advertisers/lenders destroys trust.

questions.text: Non-Discrimination in Service Delivery: Equal treatment: (1) Monitoring of service denial rates by ethnicity/region; (2) Affirmative action for remote areas; (3) Language inclusion in service delivery; (4) Cultural sensitivity training; (5) Grievance mechanism for discrimination; (6) Equal budget allocation; (7) Representation in staff.
questions.evidence_required: Service delivery stats, Budget allocation, Staff diversity data
questions.africa_specific_notes: State resources often distributed along tribal/political lines. Digital systems should be blind to tribe, but can be engineered to discriminate.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Government in SSA: Political neutrality and anti-corruption are the tests of a democratic ID system. If it rigs elections or enriches cronies, it fails.
